cell_recall.definition: mean over changing transitions of the fraction of truly-changed cells given the right value (WorldModelVerifier.cell_recall); documented as BLIND to spurious writes

change_exact_accuracy.definition: fraction of the CHANGING held-out transitions predicted exactly (WorldModelVerifier.change_accuracy); None where no changing row is held out

change_fidelity.definition: mean over changing transitions of the fraction of the UNION of (cells reality changed) and (cells the engine wrote) that the engine got right -- symmetric, so a spurious write costs what a miss costs (WorldModelVerifier.change_fidelity)

changed_cell_jaccard.definition: Jaccard between the cell-set the engine WROTE and the cell-set reality CHANGED, ignoring the values -- 'did you change the right cells'

correct_changed_cells.definition: COUNT of truly-changed cells predicted correctly (unnormalised, so it scales with how much the game moves; kept because exp6018 tested it)

exact_match_accuracy.definition: fraction of ALL held-out transitions whose predicted next grid equals the observed one exactly (WorldModelVerifier.accuracy) -- THE CONTROL, and exp6018's floored primary

grid_agreement_all.definition: 1 - normalised Hamming distance between predicted and observed next grid, over ALL held-out rows

grid_agreement_changing.definition: 1 - normalised Hamming distance, over CHANGING held-out rows only

object_inventory_jaccard.definition: multiset Jaccard over TRANSLATION-INVARIANT object hashes -- 'did you get the object inventory right', ignoring where each object ended up

object_match_iou.definition: mean over changing transitions of the pixel-count-weighted F1 of best same-colour object-to-object pixel-IoU between the predicted and observed next grid -- GRADED per-object correctness (an object off by one pixel scores ~0.97, not 0)

object_match_recall.definition: the recall half of object_match_iou (true objects matched), blind to invented objects

object_positional_jaccard.definition: multiset Jaccard over (object hash, bbox top-left) -- object inventory AND position, all-or-nothing per object

spurious_changed_cells.definition: COUNT of cells the engine wrote that are not the observed value; minimised trivially by an engine that writes nothing, which is why it is reported and not recommended
